answer: No. Your dad can give you a power of attorney using form NW-POA-2, which he can sign electronically without a notary. Only Georgia still requires a notary, and Virginia doesn't. NW-POA-2 replaced the older notarized form NW-POA-1 on February 1, 2026. NW-POA-1 was retired, and ones signed before that date were only accepted until June 30, 2026, so your dad should use NW-POA-2. Bring the signed form, your own photo ID and the car's documents to the appointment. Keep in mind that a power of attorney ends if the person who signed it dies.
